Use the model above to solve the following multiplication problem. You do not need to simplify your answer.

$\frac{4}{7}\times \frac{2}{3}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Since we need to multiply by $\frac{2}{3}$, we split the whole into $3$ equal parts horizontally and ensure that $2$ of the parts remain shaded.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130839/assets/da5df2aa46309b3d1f3b8786ebf993c33342a8b4d6267338b512c0dea3227955.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\frac{8}{21}$ of the whole.

Therefore,

$$
\frac{4}{7}\times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{8}{21}.
$$
